msItem.title: Exhortation to nuns
msItem.incipit: My dear susterys Mary and Anne wyth all the other devoȝth dyscyples of the scole of cryste in your monastery of Amysbury be grace and the blessyng of oure lorde euyr lastyng. Amen. Remembryng and consyderyng your good and relygyouse desyres to haue hadde sum goostly comforte & som maner off instructyon of me nowe att þe tyme of your professyon

(fol. 4r) Veni sequere me et habebis thesaurum in celo. Thes wordes be to sey in englysshe Cum and folow me and thow shall haue a tresure yn heuyn. His is made mencyon in the gospell wher I tooke thes wordes to trete of that for the goode and hoolsum doctrine
msItem.explicit: he of his ynfynyt goodnes grawnt you wych is kyng of virgynnes and spowse also, the crowne & reward of all wel lyuynge peopull oure lord ihesus christus. Amen.
msItem.note: Addressed to nuns of Amesbury, loosely structured as a sermon on Luke 18:22, the text begins with religious renunciation of the secular world, quoting the vow of profession at fol. 10r. Text is lost after fol. 10. The remaining sections deal with the three virtues of obedience (fols. 10r-13r, beginning of this section lost), poverty (fols. 13r-20r), and chastity (fols. 20r-26v), and the vow of profession (fols. 26v-28v) which is quoted, translated and expounded. The conclusion (fols. 28v-30r) returns to the theme Habebis thesaurum in celo. Extracts from the vow of profession name Christine as prioress (fol. 27v), i.e. Christine Fauntleroy who occurs between 1509 and 1520 (Heads of Religious Houses).
Fol. 30v blank except for later pen-trials.

'Thomas Wodlove' (?), fol. 11v; other names, scribbles and pen-trials in the margins and on the endleaves, many illegible.
